Expectation1: Provide guidance and wisdom based on life experience
Situation1: The grandparent notices their grandchild seems to be feeling lost or discouraged about a personal matter.
Situation2: They occasionally tidy up visible clutter and do light cleaning in shared spaces.
Story: I was dusting the living room shelves, careful not to disturb the family photos, when I noticed my granddaughter curled up on the couch, her eyes red and distant. My heart ached to sit beside her, to offer the comfort and advice she might need. As a grandparent, I felt the pull to share my own stories of struggle and hope, to let her know she wasn’t alone. But the clock on the wall reminded me of my other role—housekeeping cleaner. I was expected to keep the house spotless, and I’d already fallen behind on the kitchen and bathroom. My employer valued efficiency and thoroughness, and I knew I couldn’t afford to lose this job. Yet, every sweep of the duster felt heavier as I watched my granddaughter’s silent struggle. The urge to drop everything and be there for her warred with the pressure to finish my work. I stood frozen, torn between the wisdom I longed to share and the duties I was paid to perform, feeling the weight of both expectations pressing in on me.
